exchanges.question: Can you quantify the encouraging April trends quarter to date? And what specific elements of Fernando Machado's broad QSR experience do you expect him to bring to Chipotle?
exchanges.answer: Rymer: there was a nice step up in April, partly the Easter shift (Easter about two weeks earlier than the prior year) but mostly Cilantro Lime Sauce, which is outperforming Red Chimichurri with incidence about 2x, plus the rewards relaunch; no number given. Boatwright: a comprehensive search found Machado, valued for his global brand-building record and love of the brand, and his vision for the next chapter of advertising was groundbreaking.

exchanges.question: What was the comp cadence through the quarter and what does the guide embed for Q2? Separately, what membership growth is seen and is the loyalty revamp aimed at new, lapsed or existing members?
exchanges.answer: Rymer: January saw protein menu strength (double-digit increase in double protein and single tacos) with weather costing about 100 basis points to the quarter; February improved further with Chicken al Pastor (highest incidence of its three launches); March softened around the start of the Iran conflict; April stepped up. Q2 comps are expected around +1%, including a modest lift from Chipotle Honey Chicken. Boatwright: since the relaunch there has been about a 25% uplift in new members entering the funnel, with lapsed users reactivated and engagement deepened via Rewards on Repeat.

exchanges.question: Is the base case that comps accelerate through the year given LTOs and protein windows leave a lasting lift? And will new, not just familiar, LTOs matter more going forward?
exchanges.answer: He said that is exactly right: the demand map refresh showed consumers wanted more frequent innovation, so LTO cadence has doubled, digital engagement was addressed with the app relaunch, and culturally relevant marketing will increase with Machado. New center-of-the-plate protein LTOs are in process or test, with a few more to test late in the year to inform the 2027 strategy, mixing tried and true favorites occasionally with new items.

exchanges.question: What are the traffic and mix components of the comp and the mix outlook? And what specifically is changing in hospitality?
exchanges.answer: Rymer: on a 0.5% comp, transactions were up about 60 basis points, check down about 10 basis points, price about 90 basis points and mix a drag of about 100 basis points (lower group size, rewards redemptions, BYOC cannibalization, protein cups and single tacos, offset by extra meat and sides); mix should be closer to flat in Q2 thanks to Cilantro Lime Sauce, with H2 dependent on LTOs and sauces. Boatwright: customers want more hospitality than at any time since COVID; after the All Managers Conference he cites better staffing KPIs, best app model levels in years, GM turnover at historical lows and rising taste and GSAT scores.

exchanges.question: With a pricing perception issue over the last year or two, how much will Machado integrate value and price points into marketing and what could that look like?
exchanges.answer: Open to testing many ideas without handicapping Machado, but nothing that detracts from brand health. Chipotle charges a very fair price, has underpriced the industry for a second consecutive year, and is still at a 20%-30% discount to fast casual peers with a widening gap, giving pricing flexibility. Examples are the $3.50 taco entry price point and a test in a market in a couple of weeks of a Happier Hour from two to five with tacos at $2.50.

exchanges.question: Are the gaps converging in transaction growth for the younger and lower/middle income cohorts that had been under pressure? And where do European unit economics stand, is it an inflection point to accelerate unit growth?
exchanges.answer: Targeted, culturally relevant messaging engaged the younger consumer more in Q1 than over the last year, with an uptick across all ages and income cohorts; no convergence data given. On Europe, margin is now in the double-digit range with 40% ROI in year two on new restaurants; Chipotle needs to look for real estate more meaningfully in Central London and Germany and is released to go as quickly as it can.

exchanges.question: Can marketing be localized given where competition (chicken, Mexican, bowls) is growing? And were new unit volumes a touch light in Q1?
exchanges.answer: Boatwright: a deep dive in New York and Florida showed competitor openings cause some cannibalization in the first six months that recovers in months six to eight, with competitors bringing more consumers to the trade area; impact is low and national return on ad spend works hardest, so localizing would be costly. Rymer: new restaurant productivity is about 80%, as in the last couple of years, and Q1 openings may simply have been weighted later in the quarter.

exchanges.question: Is the delivery premium hurting value scores versus in-store? And how much more labor investment is needed at the restaurant level to address staffing pushback?
exchanges.answer: Testing across DoorDash and Uber showed different usage patterns; Chipotle prices, even with an elevated marketplace premium, are below peers in the channel, delivery ticked up again but remains in the teens, and order ahead surpassed 20% in the quarter. Arlie Sisson starts next week and will review third-party aggregators for the back half. On labor, there is more opportunity to invest: HEAP, Chipotle Kitchen, GM Assistant and Ava Cado free hours that are reinvested, and manager coverage of lunch and dinner peaks is a challenge being addressed.

exchanges.question: What is the shape of margins in the second half as pricing and inflation converge? And has the comp gap versus control restaurants with the equipment widened, and what is the rollout pace to 2,000?
exchanges.answer: Rymer: H1 is the period of most margin pressure (Q1 pricing 0.9% versus inflation in the mid 3% range); H2 inflation drops as beef is lapped and pricing ticks up, so the dislocation should be minimal by year end. Boatwright: equipment restaurants show comp lift of 200-400 basis points; 600 restaurants today and 2,000 by year-end, with installs at about 30-35 per week moving to 45 per week, done overnight, and the full portfolio late 2027 or early 2028.

exchanges.question: How long until test stores show the equipment-driven comp improvement? And how is the incremental return on marketing spend (up 22% in Q1) being measured given the modest comp lift?
exchanges.answer: Boatwright: about two months (a month to become proficient and a month to hit stride). Rymer: spend supporting four LTOs and Chipotle days such as the tattoo BOGO is measured individually and returns are good, though there is still consumer noise. Boatwright: marketing has a tail, with sales overnight and brand over time, and spend will continue as long as return on ad spend is responsible and margin accretive; no return figures given.

exchanges.question: Why does Q2 guidance of a +1% comp imply a traffic decline versus Q1's gain, is it conservative? And what drove the 2025 rise in hourly turnover and what is planned beyond the equipment package to improve throughput?
exchanges.answer: Rymer: the analyst is right, the outlook is modest on Honey Chicken and other initiatives given the consumer environment, the Iran conflict and gas prices, but he believes there is upside. Boatwright: 2025 turnover was an anomaly as sales decelerated and hours fell, plus hard decisions on hiring for hospitality; Q1 turnover is back to historical lows. The throughput-beyond-equipment question was not separately addressed.
